sents.t: On October 10th, I woke up at five.
I was so nervous that I could only eat half a banana.
At the starting line, there were two thousand runners.
Jasmine found me and gave me some last advice.
She told me to start slowly and to drink water at every station.
She said that the hardest part would be mile ten.
For the first five miles, I felt amazing.
Rosa, Max, and Lily were cheering at mile three, and Mia and Leo were giving high fives to every runner.
But Jasmine was right.
At mile ten, my legs felt like stone.
A woman next to me asked me if I was OK.
I told her that I didn’t think I could finish.
She said she had felt the same way in her first race, and that I should only focus on the next lamp post.
So I did.
One lamp post, then another, then another.
When I turned the last corner, I heard people shouting my name.
Carlos was standing on a bench, and Emma had come from Chicago to surprise me!
I crossed the finish line in two hours and seven minutes, and a volunteer put a medal around my neck.
Later, Rosa told me that she had cried when she saw me finish.
I told her that I had cried too.

comp.q: Why could Sam only eat half a banana?
comp.fa: چرا سام فقط توانست نصف یک موز بخورد؟

o: to start slowly and drink water
to run fast at the start

comp.q: What does “my legs felt like stone” mean?
o: His legs were very heavy and tired.
comp.fa: «my legs felt like stone» یعنی چه؟

comp.q: What did the woman tell Sam to do?
o: focus on the next lamp post
comp.fa: آن زن به سام گفت چه کار کند؟

comp.q: Who came from Chicago to surprise Sam?
comp.fa: چه کسی از شیکاگو آمد تا سام را غافلگیر کند؟
